comment: Status rules (docs/RELEASES.md): 'available' only after the file was installed and tested on a real device; 'preview' runs with the stated limitation; 'soon' has no file. Sizes and SHA-256 are computed by tools/build.py, never typed.

platforms.name: Android
platforms.text: The phone app. Pairs as an Xbox Wireless Controller over Bluetooth, so a Mac needs nothing installed; works in games and in browser cloud gaming (Safari and Chrome see a standard gamepad). Black-glass controller lit in each game's colour, gyro aim, turbo buttons, Controller Lock, games you can share by QR code, GameCube and arcade-stick layouts, a Quick Settings tile and per-game shortcuts, move and resize any button, and a connection check that says why the computer can't be reached. Open the file on your phone and allow installing from your browser when Android asks. Updates earlier versions in place.
platforms.tested: This exact file (signed release 0.2.3) was installed over 0.2.2 on a realme 12 5G (Android 16) and kept its settings. On the phone: the connection check opened, Bluetooth controller mode started after the app asked Android to turn Bluetooth on, and turning the mode off gave the phone its own Bluetooth name back. The Bluetooth controller itself is unchanged from 0.2.2, which delivered A, B, X, Y and the D-pad to a MacBook Air (macOS 27.0.1) in GameController. Customise was checked in an earlier 0.2.3 release build on an Android 16 emulator (its code is unchanged since).

platforms.name: Mac
platforms.meta: macOS 13 or newer · Apple silicon and Intel · keyboard & mouse mode
platforms.text: The phone plays your Mac games as keyboard and mouse: left stick is WASD, A is Space, the right stick moves the mouse, the triggers click. Allow it once under Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Games that only accept a controller can't see it yet — that needs a permission from Apple. Not notarized yet: after the first launch is blocked, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.
platforms.tested: Version 0.1.1, installed from this DMG and launched on macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon). Keyboard & mouse mode passed a live test: all 18 keys, pointer movement both ways on both axes, and both clicks, in order.

platforms.name: iPhone
platforms.text: Free with your own Apple ID. New in 0.2: the black-glass controller lit in each game's colour, a games row and a Now playing home screen. Add it to AltStore and it refreshes and updates itself; or install the file once with Sideloadly. Step-by-step in the guide.
platforms.tested: This exact file (0.2.1) was re-signed with a regular Apple ID the way Sideloadly does, installed and launched on an iPhone 15 running iOS 27.0.1, and stayed running. The same app passed the 20-of-20 touch-accuracy UI test on an iPhone 18 Pro simulator.

platforms.name: Windows
platforms.text: Games see an Xbox 360 controller, with rumble back to your phone. On first run, press Install driver once: it adds the free, signed ViGEmBus driver (Windows asks for permission). Not code-signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.

platforms.name: Linux
platforms.text: Games see a standard Xbox 360-style controller. The package adds a rule so your desktop session can create it — log out and back in once after installing.
